transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-01 16:00 UTC / Duration 37m
Attendees: Jenn Harper (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood CSM); Priya Sharma (CTO, Helion), Mark Li (Sr ML Eng), Dana Ortiz (Security Eng), Connor Blake (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery re: Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token for Helion's in-app assistant. Discussion covered Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, security needs (VPC/KMS/SOC2), latency/cost tradeoffs, and immediate next steps to spin up a trial and run a small benchmark.

00:00:03 Jenn: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, um quick round of intros, i'm jen harper, AE on the PLG team at Redwood.
00:00:10 Priya: hi jen, priya here, CTO at Helion. we've got mark and dana on the call as well.
00:00:15 Mark: hey all, quick note we mostly own the infra and ml infra side.
00:00:20 Miguel: miguel ortiz here, solutions engineer, i'll cover performance and dedicated questions.
00:00:28 Connor: connor from product, excited to see what the quickstart looks like.
00:00:34 Jenn: awesome, goal for today is to understand your use case, constraints, time-to-first-token expectations, and to show the path to a PLG quickstart - like free credits, onboarding, and how fast you can get to an API key and first token.
00:00:46 Priya: sounds good. at a high level we want an in-app assistant for our ops console, low latency for short prompts, and strict data controls. we need to decide if hosted is ok or we have to go dedicated/private.
00:01:02 Jenn: ok, can you tell us about current stack and traffic patterns?
00:01:08 Mark: we're on aws, EKS, most requests are short - averaging 20 to 60 tokens per request - burst-y during deployments, maybe 200 RPS peak across all customers, but per-tenant it's lower.
00:01:22 Dana: security-wise we need KMS integration, audit logs, and ideally VPC peering or private-link. SOC2 is a checklist item for us.
00:01:33 Miguel: that fits a lot of customers. for PLG/self-serve you can try Redwood Hosted first - we give free credits, spin up an API key within minutes, SDKs, and you can run quick time-to-first-token tests. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but if you need network isolation or KMS-managed keys we have Dedicated and Private options.
00:01:55 Priya: what's the typical time to first token on hosted? like from sign-up to a token?
00:02:02 Jenn: usually under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart and use the SDK; with streaming enabled you can get progressive outputs. the free credits let you run perf tests so you can measure p50/p95 latencies.
00:02:14 Mark: do you provide sample load scripts or benchmark sheets? we like to reproduce latencies ourselves.
00:02:20 Miguel: yep, we have a perf benchmark spreadsheet and a small k6/locust script we share in the quickstart repo. i'll attach that. note that latency varies by model and quantization - lighter quantized variants are cheaper but can add a few ms.
00:02:36 Connor: for the quickstart, what's the onboarding flow and are there any friction points for engineers?
00:02:41 Jenn: sign up, verify email, create an API key, SDK install, run the quickstart notebook. free credits are applied to your account; with the SDK you can go from zero to first-token in a dev environment in ~5-10 minutes. if you want to push to prod we'll talk about Dedicated reservations or our Private VPC offering.
00:02:57 Dana: for compliance we need logs forwarded to our SIEM and the ability to control retention. does hosted support that?
00:03:05 Miguel: hosted offers audit logs and configurable retention; for SIEM we can export via syslog or S3 export. for stricter controls like customer-managed KMS and private networking, Dedicated or Private are the right fit. Dedicated can be configured with private networking and KMS integrations depending on contract.
00:03:22 Priya: timeline: we have a customer pilot in 6 weeks. we'd like to validate quality and latency in 2 weeks. is that feasible with hosted?
00:03:29 Jenn: absolutely. quickstart + free credits is designed for that. you can spin up, run the sample benchmark, and report back p50/p95. if you need more realistic throughput we can set up a small dedicated pool as a POC.
00:03:42 Mark: do you support model pinning and can we compare versions? we need deterministic rollouts.
00:03:47 Miguel: yes - version pinning, canary rollouts, and A/B testing are supported via our rollout configs. you can pin specific model revisions and route a percentage of traffic.
00:03:56 Priya: any gotchas with KV cache or streaming when we move to dedicated?
00:04:01 Miguel: primarily tuning. Dedicated gives you more control over sequence lengths, KV cache sizing, and batching. sometimes the auto-batching on hosted is fine but for high throughput low-latency cases we tune the runtime kernels and batching parameters.
00:04:15 Mark: cost question - are the hosted per-token rates fixed or volume discounts? and how does dedicated pricing work?
00:04:21 Jenn: hosted is usage-based per-token with volume tiers. Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing - monthly commit for GPU pools plus a smaller per-token compute fee. we can share an example sheet for a workload similar to yours.
00:04:33 Dana: security question - do you have SOC2 and can we get pen test evidence?
00:04:37 Miguel: yes SOC2 Type II, certs and security pack included in the docs we send. for enterprise pilots we can provide redacted pen test summaries and work with your procurement on any required questionnaires.
00:04:49 Priya: data residency - some customers need EU-only. does hosted let us pick region?
00:04:54 Jenn: yes hosted regions available in NA and EU, with select APAC regions. Dedicated and Private allow you to fully control region and networking.
00:05:04 Connor: ok, for the free credits - is there anything the engineering team needs to prepare beyond a list of prompts and some test keys?
00:05:10 Jenn: no major prep - sample prompt sets, a small corpus for evals, credentials for sign-up. we'll provide a test harness and the perf scripts. the quickstart notebook also includes a sample eval harness.
00:05:20 Mark: regarding inference models, do you host open weights or Redwood-managed models? we prefer open models.
00:05:26 Miguel: we host a curated catalog - many open models are available and we also surface Redwood-verified performance profiles. you can bring-your-own-model in Private deployments.
00:05:34 Priya: if we start with hosted and then move to dedicated, how smooth is the migration?
00:05:38 Miguel: we've done this many times - same API surface and SDK, you change endpoints/pinning and rollout policies. data flows and model versions can be preserved; stateful KV caches are handled per deployment. migration docs are in the runbook.
00:05:53 Jenn: quick note, some transcription: sorry, not relevant.
00:05:56 Mark: uh, question on rate limits and quotas for the free trial?
00:06:00 Jenn: trials have soft quotas to prevent abuse but they are sufficient for perf tests; we can temporarily raise limits for POC if you request.
00:06:08 Dana: any concerns about PHI/PII, we might be pushing logs into the model for summarization?
00:06:14 Miguel: we recommend token redaction in the prompt and field-level scrubbing. for higher assurance use Private with customer-managed KMS and stricter retention. we also support in-flight encryption and optional HSM integrations for keys.
00:06:28 Priya: ok, good. what would you recommend as first experiment?
00:06:32 Jenn: a three-step quickstart: 1) create trial account + apply free credits, 2) run the quickstart notebook and the perf script to capture p50/p95 for the primary prompt set, 3) share results - we'll help interpret and propose Hosted vs Dedicated POC.
00:06:46 Mark: timeline sounds good - we'll try to run step 1 today and step 2 early next week.
00:06:51 Connor: sounds good.
00:06:55 Miguel: i'll also include a short doc comparing latency/cost tradeoffs for the typical Helion workload and a note on batch tuning and quantization profiles.
00:07:05 Jenn: any blockers on your side for starting sign-up?
00:07:09 Priya: only procurement for the pilot account if we need to sign an enterprise agreement but for initial trial i think we're ok.
00:07:16 Dana: will need to coordinate with security to review SOC2 pack but that's subsequent.
00:07:22 Jenn: cool. quick recap of action items and owners, and then we'll open it up for any last questions.
00:07:28 Miguel: action items: i'll get the perf scripts and dedicated comparison doc over.
00:07:32 Jenn: i'll send credits link and quickstart guide, and mike, sorry, mark, you'll get the sample prompt eval.
00:07:39 Mark: thanks.
00:07:41 Priya: one more thing - do you have examples of customers who started hosted then moved to dedicated? any case study?
00:07:48 Miguel: yes i'll share a short case blurb (anonymized) that shows migration and cost improvements after tuning.
00:07:56 Jenn: ok, last quick troubleshooting note - sometimes the SDK needs an upgrade for streaming on older node versions, but we'll include the note in the quickstart.
00:08:05 Connor: perfect.
00:08:07 Jenn: all right unless there's anything else we'll wrap. thanks everyone.
00:08:12 Priya: thanks all. bye.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: quickstart notebook link (sent post-call), perf benchmark spreadsheet (attached), SOC2 pack (link), Dedicated vs Hosted comparison doc (to be sent).

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts present: minor name mismatches, dropped filler words, occasional mis-heard acronyms like 'K-V cache' vs KV cache.
